description.narrative: The programme “Network for diversity and inclusion” will be implemented by Hivos and eight local partner organisations during a four-year-long period. The Swedish contribution to the project is SEK 32 000 000. Hivos is responsible for forwarding the funds to the third-party organisations along with providing administrative, technical and strategic support. There are two specific objectives of the programme related to achievements in societal change, and one strategic objective related to strenghtening of civil society. The first objective is to support the state and its institutions in assuming their role as duty bearers guaranteeing the citizens' rights as established in national and international law, particularly in sexual and reproductive health rights with a strong focus on LGBTIQ-rights, access to justice and labour rights. The second objective is to guarantee girls, boys, adolescents and youth an effective access to comprehensive sexual education. The third objective is to strengthen the third-party organisations to make them more independent and able to act in alliances with other civil society organisation to achieve their goals.

HBTIQ-personers rättigheter och kvinnors och flickors tillgång till SRHR skyddas i Guatemalas lagstiftning och i internationella överenskommelser som landet ingått. Trots detta utsätts HBTIQ-personer för kränkningar, våld och diskriminering. Likaså kränks flickor och kvinnors sexuella och reproduktiva rättigheter, tillgången till sexuell och reproduktiv hälsa är i praktiken begränsad (SRHR).
Programmet ”Nätverk för mångfald och inkludering i Guatemala” kommer att genomföras av HIVOS, en internationell civilsamhällsorganisation med huvudkontor i Nederländerna, i samarbete med åtta partnerorganisationer. Programmet har ett trefaldigt syfte: •Att genom påverkan, ansvarsutkrävande, konstruktiva förslag och samarbete stödja statliga institutioner att i högre grad garantera lagstadgade rättigheter, med fokus på SRHR och rättsväsendets förmåga att agera mot kränkningar, våld och diskriminering (inklusive arbetsrättslig sådan). •Att förbättra tillgången till allsidig sexualundervisning i enlighet med nationella lagar och strategier. •Att stärka civilsamhällsorganisationer som verkar för dessa rättigheter och deras förmåga att skapa nätverk som arbetar mot gemensamma mål.
Det svenska bidraget till programmet, 32 miljoner kronor, kommer att bidra till att bedriva kommunikationsarbete, ta fram forskning och evidensbaserade policyförslag, utbilda och informera, samt ge rättsligt och psykologiskt stöd åt personer som fått sina rättigheter kränkta. Att stärka de lokala organisationernas system, förvaltning och interndemokrati är ett annat viktigt inslag.
Att programmet omfattar både SRHR, HBTIQ-rättigheter, kvinnors och flickors egenmakt, samt maskulinitet är ett nytt grepp som kan öka effekterna av de olika organisationernas verksamhet och dessutom öppna upp för bredare allianser mellan organisationer som traditionellt inte samarbetat.
De åtta partnerorganisationer har närvaro i fyra av Guatemalas 17 regioner, både huvudstadsregionen, och regioner med en hög andel urfolk och som drabbas särskilt hårt av mödradödlighet, sexuellt våld och tonårsgraviditeter.
Dialog och strategisk kommunikation kommer att samordnas med Nederländernas ambassad i Costa Rica, som finansierar ett regionalt HIVOS-program på samma tema.

The rights of LGBTIQ persons and women's and girls' access to SRHR are protected in Guatemalan legislation and in international agreements entered into by the country. Despite this, LGBTIQ persons are subjected to violations, violence and discrimination. Similarly, girls and women's sexual and reproductive rights are violated, in practice, access to sexual and reproductive health is limited (SRHR).
The programme "Network for diversity and inclusion in Guatemala" will be implemented by HIVOS, an international civil society organisation with headquarters in the Netherlands, in collaboration with eight partner organisations. The programme has a three-fold purpose: • Through influence, accountability, constructive proposals and cooperation, support state institutions to better guarantee statutory rights, focusing on the SRHR and the judiciary's ability to act against violations, violence and discrimination (including labor law). • To improve access to comprehensive sexual education in accordance with national laws and strategies. • Strengthening civil society organisations that work for these rights and their ability to create networks that work towards common goals.
The Swedish grant to the program, SEK 32 million, will help carry out communication work, produce research and evidence-based policy proposals, educate and inform, as well as provide legal and psychological support to persons who have been violated. Strengthening the systems, administration and internal democracy of local organisations is another important element.
The fact that the programme encompasses both SRHR, LGBTIQ rights, women's and girls 'empowerment, and masculinity is a new approach that can increase the effects of the various organisations' activities and also open up to broader alliances between organisations that have not traditionally collaborated.
The eight partner organisations have a presence in four of Guatemala's 17 regions, both the metropolitan region, and regions with a high proportion of indigenous peoples, who are particularly hard hit by maternal mortality, sexual violence and teenage pregnancies.
Dialogue and strategic communication will be coordinated with the Netherlands Embassy in Costa Rica, which funds a regional HIVOS programme on the same theme.

Some of the results reported by Hivos include reaching 2,041 LGBTIQ persons through educational outreach with "My body, my territory" program and monthly thematic workshops. Hivos local partners participated in citizen action against conservative law initiatives which sought to limit rights of women, girls and LGBTIQ persons fundamental rights; in the end, the law initiatives were not approved by Congress.
Guate Diversa e Inclusiva (GDI) local partners received organizational capacity building which included communication, resource mobilization, finance, strategic planning, political advocacy, and financial-administrative processes, among others.
In result related to improved knowledge by state employees and authorities of rights of LGBTIQ persons, 813 state employees/authorities received training, capacity building and sensitizing in sexual and reproductive health rights with emphasis on sexual diversity. The organization Visibles implemented a course at School of Psychology at San Carlos National University on depathologization of sexual diversity and gender identity, affirmative psychology and human rights of LGBTIQ persons. Additionally, personnel of Guatemalan Institute of Migration received training on these issues.
In Quetzaltenango, sensitizing and training was carried out with public sector employees and authorities of Ministry of Labour, Public Prosecutors Office, the National Police, Institute of the Victim, Ministry of Education and the Health Ministry on sexual diversity and human rights, stigma and discrimination, sexually transmitted diseases, diversity and discrimination in puberty and adolescence, and statistics on violence against LGBTIQ persons.
As to improved action by responsible state institutions, the organization Visibles signed a Letter of Understanding with the Presidential Commission against Racism and Discrimination (CODISRA) giving a role to Visibles in capacity building related to discrimination. Visibles also presented 2 studies on labor inclusion and discrimination in the workplace.
In strategic objective 2 related to access to comprehensive sexual and reproductive health education in 4 prioritized departments: Guatemala, Quetzaltenango, Quiche and Huehuetenango, GDI reached a total of 11,662 children and youth through educational activities on SRHR and access to services. Other actions in objective 2 supported participation in collective actions to guarantee access to Integral Sexual Education (ISE) for youth, support to Sexual and Reproductive Health Observatory (OSAR), sensitizing and forming 1,853 public servants of Ministry of Health and Ministry of Education on ISE, preparation of educational toolbox for teaching about sexual and reproductive health rights with focus on prevention of sexual violence against children and youth, participation by OSAR in 2 working groups of the Special Cabinet of Social Development (1. working group on prevention of pregnancies in adolescents and 2. working group on prevention of sexual violence) which contributed to an analysis of sexual violence against children and of creating a road map to provide adequate attention to pregnant girls under 14, and providing technical assistance by OSAR to National Working Group for National Plan of Prevention of Pregnancies in Adolescents PLANEA.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
